ctx.x: "Chinatown, my China, China-town, one of those things. There was a guy named Nesbitt that did a gang of arranging for McKinney's Cottonpickers. This was even before Don Redman (unintelligible). Nesbitt, he was a trumpet player. Man, he was -- he got real popular, as he was an arranger and everything. And he was the one that brought that old tune back, man, Chinatown, you know. He made arrangements for Fletcher like mad. And then the thing happened. He got so that he was an excessive drinker, unfortunately. This…

ruined his career.
But I'm going to tell you something that happened once. He brought an arrangement to Fletcher one time. I've forgotten the name of the tune, or the arrangement, whatever it was. But I know what went on. The band got to playing, and to man, and they played the first chorus, just started swinging and everything, and all of a sudden his mind must have snapped somewhere along the way. It went off into another key, mistakes and all this, and it wasn't the same tune and all that. You know? And the…
